[b]Learning and Doing[/b]

Tartakum has decided to open up itself to the world, beginning with Qianxun. The Energy Cooperation Group, for its part, has began arriving en masse towards Tartakums coastal cities to set up offices and collate Tarta reports on oil reserves overlooking its waters. ECG Chairman Kang Hongxin would participate in the initial round of investigations together with the ECG Central Commission, a 108-man body of economic specialists, military officers, labor leaders, environmentalists, and socialist theoreticians that was to aid Tartakum in reinvigorating its stagnant economy. Much of its body would be constituted by Elseyro-Vespurians from Qianxuns foreign companies, with only around 41% actually coming from Qianxun itself.

Victoria Strand, the CEO of SummitONE Technologies and board member for Dearborn Bank, would be selected to serve as the head of the ECG Central Commission, coordinating the movement of its field investigation teams, consolidating reports and statistics, and creating the final paper that was to be submitted to the Tarta government. The entire process would take roughly a week, with foreign advisors working around the clock, interviewing Tarta government agencies and combing through academic papers, while the drafting and revision of the final report would take a further three days, culminating at last in the creation of the Strand Memoranda (officially entitled Economic Conditions in the Republic of Tartakum), a consultative document that would be presented to the Tartees on the 10th of November, 2025.

[b]The Strand Memoranda[/b]

[list]

[b][u]Confidential[/u]

Economic Conditions in the Republic of Tartakum
November 2025[/b]

[list]

[b]BACKGROUND [/b] The Tarta economy maintains one of the highest GDP per capita in East Shamat at around C$26,000. Despite this, income inequality and limited economic diversification hampers its economic growth, with wealth largely concentrated in a limited number of industries related to agriculture and manufacturing. As of the creation of this memoranda, current Tarta industries rely on production through cheap labor and low capital without facilitating further investments into the necessary instruments to facilitate technological innovation. Furthermore, a massive, antiquated, and inefficient agricultural market remains prominent, generating very little surplus value for its amount of labor.

[b]Oil and gas[/b]. The primary economic project currently being implemented is the Energy Cooperation Group (ECG), a state-run corporate monopoly created jointly by the governments of Tartakum and Qianxun, done in partnership with the Almstedt Corporation and the University of Qianxun Project 661 to manage all assets associated with the Tarta oil reserves in the Bay of Tartakum. Currently, the ECG is in the process of fabricating and integrating a network of about 19 semi-submersible oil platforms (oil rigs) situated across the Bay. Until more favorable conditions can be found, the hulls for these oil rigs are to be placed under construction at the ECG Development Yard in the Rolena, while the deck modules will be dispersed to various Tarta constrution companies located near the coast. Tartakum lacks the infrastructure to construct specialist components like blowout preventers, top drive systems, and draw works, which shall be constructed at Qianxun and then shipped to there.

[b]The big lift[/b]. Tarta merchant vessels are to transport these modules to integration yards overlooking the Bay of Tartakum to be integrated. Sheerleg cranes will need to be provisioned to place the deck modules onto the oil rig hulls in precise, big lifts. Once secured, the oil rigs must be welded together, tested for functionality, and then towed to their designated oil reserve for drilling and production. Put together, this process will take place over a period of around six (6) years and require a budget of around C$1.9 billion. Considering the ECGs current capital, only five (5) of the 19 available oil reserves may be accessed at this time.

[b]ECG flotation[/b]. The ECG has accomplished initial flotation to raise further capital. In accordance with agreements set by the ECG Central Commission with Dearborn Bank and the Tarta Chamber of Commerce, the corporations initial valuation was raised to $720 million on flotation with 60,000,000 shares priced at C$12.00 each. 10,000,000 of these shares would be sold at flotation together with 2,500,000 shares sold by investors. In total, ~C$120 million would be generated on flotation, with the final trade of the day finishing at a final price of C$15.79, setting ECG valuation at ~$947 million.

[b]Sovereign wealth fund[/b]. While waiting revenue from ECGs projects, the Qianxun Government recommends that Tartakum make provision for the development of a sovereign wealth fund (SWF) that is to hold majority ownership in the ECG and all other oil and gas projects to be operated within Tartakum. In accordance with the recommendation of the ECG Central Commission, this SWF must only be replenished with capital from ECG and other oil revenues. It furthermore recommends that only 3% of the SWFs total valuation may be transferred to the Tarta national budget per year to prevent depletion. We recommend that the budget transfer of the SWF be set at the following parameters: (1) 50% on human capital, (2) 30% on physical capital, and (3) 20% on direct investment in other oil and gas enterprises.

[b]Special economic zones[/b]. Two new special economic zones shall be created to encourage foreign direct investment in Tartakum. The ECG Central Commission recommends Rolena or another nearby city to encourage technology and services, as well as the uninhabited island west of Tartakum to serve as a new coastal port for export-oriented manufacturing. In their capacity as special economic zones (SEZs), we will require that these two sites have (1) uninterrupted power supply through a power plant which Qianxun is willing to supply, (2) high bandwidth internet infrastructure, (3) a consolidated land use and zoning agency that shall enable corporations to obtain their required permits, licenses, and Tarta bank accounts within a reasonable time frame, and (4) autonomous corporate laws to encourage labor contracts and expedited repatriation of corporate profits.

[b]Advisory mission[/b]. At the present time, the ECG Central Commission serves as the main point of contact between the governments of Tartakum and Qianxun. However, as we anticipated the growth of new industries, the government of Qianxun recommends the creation of an advisory mission, staffed by Qianxun specialists, which are to embed themselves within Tartas ministries to ensure that all economic projects remain efficiently-run and transparently-governed.

[b]CONCLUSION [/b] ECG projects are expected to aid in the growth of the Tarta economy, though it remains undercapitalized to accomplish drilling in all available oil reserves within the timeline provided by the Tarta government. While awaiting revenues, Qianxun expects Tartakum to make provision with its available legislative mechanisms to prepare an SWF with which to receive oil revenues for reinvestment in other industries. Our regards to the Tarta government.

[/list][/list]
